source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #254 (branch fix/131-wast-harness-assertions at commit fb01564eb0d7f252d3b24da100b325d5e7d56796, the merge of the PR head 3420455b6ee3a6614cc397fc8b4023c28c20bdbc with main 4d3b77441d337a6ec8c2586c1e856b1f749be87c; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45060131072 and 45060142935 against the branch and pull-request run 45060031215, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #254 (#131, wast harness spec fidelity). The PR strengthens the wast test harness (trap/invalid reason matching, result arity, bit-exact NaN patterns) and fixes the real defects that strengthening surfaced, all of them in the telomere core library: the parser's memarg alignment check is unified on natural_align_log2 (values.rs, instruction.rs, simd_instruction.rs), the type checker now produces UnknownLabel, unknown export indices return their per-kind error variants (parser.rs), and the interpreter's rounding paths quiet signaling NaNs (runtime/vm/numeric.rs, simd.rs, superinstructions.rs). The harness changes themselves are test-only and are not linked into the embedder. Because the core library is linked into every embedder configuration except baseline, the baseline configuration is byte-identical in both profiles (4 of 28 gated series unchanged) and the growth is near-uniform across the library configurations: in the release profile, stripped file +640..+880 B and stripped .text +624..+832 B; in the release-size profile, stripped file +528..+2,000 B and stripped .text +576..+2,048 B. core-nosimd grows the least in release-size (+528 B / +576 B) because the SIMD parser and runtime paths it excludes carry part of the change. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, 'Size regression gate (#164)'.
